sentiment.instructions: On the whole, does the author of this text evaluate what it talks about favorably, unfavorably, or not at all?

positive.description: On the whole, the author evaluates what the text talks about favorably, for instance by praising, recommending, supporting or welcoming it.
examples: Not even 20 pages into Paper Towns and the book centers around the night of May 5th. I know its gonna be a good one now!

neutral.description: The author does not evaluate anything, or the evaluation is too weak or unclear to call favorable or unfavorable.
examples: I may be sleep deprived but I promise you that some kid at Dunkin today looked like a sprout.

negative.description: On the whole, the author evaluates what the text talks about unfavorably, for instance by criticizing, mocking, opposing or complaining about it.
examples: The tragedy of only thinking up hilarious tweets for the Summer Olympics now is that in four years there may be no place for them.
